nodes.description: WNT5A signals through receptor complexes including ROR2 and Frizzled to Dishevelled and noncanonical pathways. Founding embryonic assays showed reduced activity, whereas C83S cell assays retained JNK-PCP activation and showed receptor-dependent changes in canonical antagonism. Neither a universal decrease in every branch nor a universal gain is established.

evidence.reference_title: Robinow syndrome skeletal phenotypes caused by the WNT5AC83S variant are due to dominant interference with chondrogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Strikingly, WNT5AC83S consistently caused a delay in ossification and bones were more than 50% shorter and 200% wider than controls.

nodes.description: C83S misexpression in chicken limbs disrupts Golgi-based chondrocyte orientation and Prickle localization before marked cartilage dysmorphology. This is experimental developmental cartilage, not a patient biopsy. A 2025 preprint reports spatially uniform chondrocyte misalignment in CRISPR-edited mouse embryos; its F0-only design cannot exclude mosaic or biallelic editing. Local misalignment is a morphological readout, not direct measurement of pathway activation.

evidence.reference_title: Robinow syndrome skeletal phenotypes caused by the WNT5AC83S variant are due to dominant interference with chondrogenesis.
evidence.snippet: Instead of stereotypical stacking of chondrocytes, the WNT5AC83S-infected cartilage was composed of randomly oriented chondrocytes and that had diffuse, rather than concentrated Prickle staining, both signs of disrupted planar cell polarity (PCP) mechanisms.

nodes.description: Consider growth hormone replacement when endocrine evaluation demonstrates deficiency. A small 1999 clinical series reported increased growth velocity in treated patients, but their molecular subtypes were uncharacterized. This supports selected treatment of coexisting deficiency without establishing efficacy in WNT5A-confirmed disease or correction of its developmental mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Robinow syndrome with growth hormone deficiency: treatment with growth hormone.
evidence.snippet: Recombinant human GH therapy in our patient and the three patients from the NCGS resulted in a significant increase in the growth rate per year.

evidence.reference_title: Robinow syndrome with growth hormone deficiency: treatment with growth hormone.
evidence.snippet: We propose its association with GH deficiency and that treatment with rhGH can result in a significant increase in the growth rate of these children.

nodes.description: Selected missense substitutions and in-frame variants alter the secreted WNT5A ligand. Many change conserved cysteines. Both inherited and de novo variants occur, including a reported mosaic in-frame duplication; a null allele is not assumed to produce the same dominant disorder.

evidence.reference_title: WNT5A mutations in patients with autosomal dominant Robinow syndrome.
evidence.snippet: we show that two different missense mutations in WNT5A, which result in amino acid substitutions of highly conserved cysteines, are associated with autosomal dominant Robinow syndrome

evidence.reference_title: WNT5A mutations in patients with autosomal dominant Robinow syndrome.
evidence.snippet: One mutation has been found in all living affected members of the original family described by Meinhard Robinow and another in a second unrelated patient.
